title: Airstrike hits Donetsk Regional Drama Theatre sheltering civilians in Mariupol
body:
On 16 March 2022, shortly after 10 a.m., an airstrike hit the Donetsk Regional Academic Drama Theatre in Mariupol during the siege of the city. Mariupol City Council officials said the theatre was the city's largest single air-raid shelter. Estimates of the number of people inside range from 500, cited by Human Rights Watch, to 1,200, cited by the BBC and by deputy mayor Serhiy Orlov.

Casualty estimates differ by source. The city council initially said no one had been killed, and about 130 survivors were reported rescued by 18 March. On 25 March the Mariupol City Council reported about 300 killed. The Associated Press, in an investigation published on 4 May 2022, found evidence pointing to about 600 deaths. Amnesty International, in a report of 30 June 2022, said at least a dozen people were killed and likely many more.

The OSCE concluded on 13 April 2022 that the incident was most likely a serious violation of international humanitarian law and a war crime, and said it had received no indication that Ukrainian forces destroyed the building. Amnesty International attributed the attack to Russian forces using two 500-kilogram bombs. The Russian Ministry of Defence denied responsibility and blamed the Azov Regiment for planting explosives, a claim that independent investigations have not supported.
